name: application-conditional-field-group
title: Conditional Field Group
description: Form section gated by a controlling checkbox: an indented field group reveals when checked, with a connecting rail; an optional helper description explains the fallback when unchecked.
useWhen: A form field or section is only relevant when a controlling checkbox or option is enabled (e.g. "notify me" revealing an email + frequency field).
You want to avoid showing irrelevant fields up front, reducing perceived form length.
The unchecked state has an implicit fallback worth explaining in a short helper line, rather than just disappearing silently.
avoidWhen: The revealed fields are always relevant regardless of a toggle — just show them directly without gating.
The controlling input is a multi-way select rather than a boolean checkbox — build a custom conditional render keyed off the select value instead of reusing this checkbox-driven shape.
responsiveBehavior: The revealed field group is a single indented column at all widths; the connecting rail and left padding stay fixed rather than scaling with viewport.
accessibility: The controlling checkbox and its label are a real <label>/<input> pair, so clicking the label text toggles the group.
Revealed fields are removed from the DOM when unchecked (not just visually hidden), so screen readers and tab order never encounter irrelevant, hidden-but-focusable inputs.
The fallback description text explains the unchecked behavior in words, so the consequence of leaving the box unchecked isn't left ambiguous.

variants.title: Conditional Field Group
variants.description: A checked 'Email me about product updates' group revealing Email address and Frequency fields with a connecting rail, and an unchecked 'Ship to a different address' group showing a fallback description instead.
accessibility: Revealed fields only exist in the DOM while checked, so they're never reachable by keyboard when hidden.

variants.title: Conditional Field Group (Dark)
variants.description: The same two conditional groups adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Connecting rail and revealed-field contrast remain legible against the dark surface.
